source.text: While an enemy unit is within 6" of this unit, if this unit contains one or more **BLUE HORROR** models, worsen the Leadership characteristic of models in that enemy unit by 1.

Each time this unit is selected to fight, you can select one enemy unit within **Engagement Range** of it, then select one or more **BRIMSTONE HORROR** models in this unit. For each **BRIMSTONE HORROR** model you select, roll one D6: on a 4+, that model is destroyed and that enemy unit suffers 1 **mortal wound**.

Each time this unit or an enemy unit ends a move, for each model in this unit that is within 3" of one or more enemy units, select one of those enemy units. That model in this unit is destroyed, then roll one D6: on a 2-5, that enemy unit suffers 1 **mortal wound**; on a 6, that enemy unit suffers D3 mortal wounds.
Enemy units cannot start or end an **Advance move** within 6" of this unit.

source.implements: the list import (import.js): a New Recruit JSON export becomes a list only when its faction, its one battle size (its points limit BSData's for it, and the total within it), its one detachment selection (each detachment once), its one Force Disposition (one its detachments allow), its config (Code Chivalric, known choices) and every other top-level selection (Show/Hide Options, rules references, with known choices only) are what data.js has, and every unit, with the characters attached to it (New Recruit's Leading/Supporting), has the BSData signature (signature) of a unit of a data.js list with the same faction, detachments, config and battle size, the same BSData names and the same points (BS_IDS, written by verify/import-ids.js); an option holding models is taken once; then the list as a whole: at most one Warlord (none only as a list of the app has none), each entry no more often than BSData's max per list that no modifier changes (an enhancement once, an Epic Hero once), the units adding up to the total; then the units are copied as data.js has them (a unit taken again as its copies; import-nr.js's order: role, units without a leader, the roster's order); otherwise nothing is imported and every item not recognized is listed (and a group the closest unit explains no difference of is still refused)

Import (the sheet): a refused export (or one resolve cannot read) lists every message, one per line, and nothing is kept; an imported one is kept on the phone as the export (resolved again at every start, each in a try: one that cannot be read is listed as out of date), gets an id no list has, and opens; if the phone cannot keep it, the toast says so

ref.rule: Horrors are Pink. Horrors are Blue. Where once there was one, now there are two.
ref.quote: If, at any point, this unit contains no PINK HORROR models, use the BLUE HORRORS datasheet for this unit.

source.reason: Reference sheet Blue Horrors: GW’s Blue Horrors datasheet (Faction Pack Chaos Daemons 1.2 prints it), which the Pink Horrors use once they contain no Pink Horror (“If, at any point, this unit contains no PINK HORROR models, use the BLUE HORRORS datasheet for this unit.”), built from BSData’s Blue Horrors root entry (one Blue Horror with its weapons; what BSData shows only by a condition, the Shadow Legion’s Penumbral Puppetry and Stealth, left out). It carries the Brimstone Horrors too: GW gives them no datasheet of their own, only the BLUE HORROR/BRIMSTONE HORROR profile (one stats row, 25mm), Coruscating Yellow Flames and yellow claws (“Every Brimstone Horror added to this unit using the Split ability is equipped with: …”, the carrier line) and BRIMSTONE (kwOnly). So no separate Brimstone Horrors sheet: it would repeat these rows under a datasheet GW does not print. The Pink Horrors card keeps its signed-off “(ref. only)” rows (the Blue and Brimstone Horrors its own Split adds while Pink Horrors remain).
